title: Tax Compliance in the Rental Housing Market: Evidence from a Field Experiment
title_zh: 租赁住房市场中的税收遵从：来自实地实验的证据
authors: Essi Eerola, Tuomas Kosonen, Kaisa Kotakorpi, Teemu Lyytikäinen
abstract: We study rental income tax compliance using novel third-party information and a large-scale randomized field experiment. The third-party information combines register data on the ownership and occupancy of apartments. The RCT used this new third-party information in the targeting and design of experimental treatments, and increased the propensity to report rental income and the amount of reported rental income net of expenses. Our research design also allows us to identify members of ownership networks and analyze spillover effects in tax enforcement between them. We find positive reporting spillovers. We do not find evidence of real effects on asset market transactions. (JEL C93, D83, H26, K34, R31)
abstract_zh: 我们利用新颖的第三方信息和大规模随机实地实验，对租金收入纳税遵从度展开研究。该第三方信息整合了公寓所有权与居住情况的登记数据。随机对照实验将这一新型第三方信息应用于实验干预的目标定位与设计，显著提升了租金收入的申报倾向及扣除费用后的申报金额。研究设计还使我们能够识别所有权网络成员，并分析税收执法在成员间的溢出效应。研究发现存在正向的申报溢出效应，但未发现对资产市场交易产生实质性影响的证据。（JEL分类号：C93, D83, H26, K34, R31）

title: Structural Change in Production Networks and Economic Growth
title_zh: 生产网络中的结构变化与经济增长
authors: Paul Gaggl, Aspen Gorry, Christian vom Lehn
abstract: Abstract We study structural change in production networks for intermediate inputs (inputoutput network) and new capital (investment network). For each network, we document that the share of output produced by services (relative to goods) is rising over time. While the relative prices of services that produce intermediates and consumption are rising, we find that the relative price of services that produce investment is falling over time. We then develop a multi-sector growth model to study these trends and their implications for economic growth. To match the relative price trends, inputs to intermediates production are complements and inputs to investment production are substitutes. Hence, structural change endogenously reallocates resources to the slowest growing intermediates producers and the fastest growing investment producers. Growth accounting exercises reveal that investment-specific technical change accounts for an increasing share of U.S. aggregate growth, with 20% of aggregate growth since 2000 due to investment structural change. Growth projections from our model show that structural change within investment networks alone can offset stagnating or declining growth in other sectors due to Baumol’s cost disease.
abstract_zh: 摘要 本文研究了中间投入品生产网络（投入产出网络）与资本品生产网络（投资网络）中的结构变迁。对于每个网络，我们观察到服务业产出（相对于商品）的份额随时间推移持续上升。尽管生产中间品和消费品的服务业相对价格在上升，但生产投资品的服务业相对价格却在下降。为此，我们构建了一个多部门增长模型来分析这些趋势及其对经济增长的影响。为匹配相对价格变化趋势，中间品生产投入呈现互补性，而投资品生产投入则呈现替代性。因此，结构变迁内生地将资源重新配置给增长最慢的中间品生产部门与增长最快的投资品生产部门。增长核算表明，投资专用型技术进步在美国总体增长中的贡献份额持续上升，其中2000年以来20%的总体增长源于投资结构变迁。模型增长预测显示，仅投资网络内部的结构变迁即可抵消鲍莫尔成本病导致的其他部门增长停滞或下降效应。

title: Praying for Rain
authors: José-Antonio Espín-Sánchez, Salvador Gil-Guirado, Nicholas Ryan
abstract: Abstract We study rainmaking as an instrumental religious belief. We present a model in which a religious leader tries to persuade people to believe. Praying for rain can persuade only where the hazard of rainfall during a dry spell is increasing over time, so that prayer is most likely to succeed when people most want rain. We present evidence from prayers for rain in Murcia, Spain, where the hazard rate is increasing, that the church’s prayers for rain predict rainfall over two centuries. To generalize this finding, we gather an original data set of whether ethnic groups around the world traditionally prayed for rain. We find that ethnic groups facing an increasing rainfall hazard are 47% more likely to pray for rain, consistent with our model’s prediction that societies are more likely to pray for rain where prayer is persuasive.
